description: At Sunbit, we're building financial technology that puts people first. By combining intelligent decisioning with a personalized, transparent approach, we help consumers access the payment options that are right for them while empowering merchants to build stronger customer relationships. Engineering is at the heart of how we make that happen. We build scalable distributed systems, cloud-native services, intelligent data platforms, and AI-powered solutions that enable real-time financial decisions at scale. By leveraging modern engineering practices and integrating AI into both our products and development workflows, we solve complex technical challenges, accelerate innovation, and continuously improve the way we build software. Every service, model, and architectural decision we make directly impacts our products, our customers, and the future of financial technology. The Opportunity We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager – Decisioning (Credit Risk) to own, evolve, and execute Sunbit’s risk decisioning products. This role partners closely with ML Engineers , Engineering Leads and Business Stakeholders to transition Sunbit from product-specific silos into a generic, high-velocity engine powering Card, BNPL, and emerging products. Blending strategic oversight with hands-on, rigorous program execution, you will turn complex risk logic into scalable, explainable platforms. You’ll own both long-range quarterly planning and sprint execution- defining who we approve, on what terms, and at what expected loss- while ensuring strict alignment with Sunbit’s risk portfolios, regulatory requirements, and long term unit economics. This role requires strong judgment, deep analytical thinking and meticulous detail standards. Our Vision We believe in a "win-win" future where personalized decisioning empowers real people in the real world to get the most for their hard-earned money. By moving away from "one-size-fits-all" credit and toward precision-driven finance, we ensure that a car repair, a dental visit, or an everyday purchase never becomes a financial burden. Your Mission As the Program Manager , your mission is to drive an advanced, adaptable decisioning platform that eliminates financial waste and prepares Sunbit for its next stage of hyper-growth. You will drive the delivery of core systems that determine how we approve, price, and manage risk—turning complex data into fair, instant, and transparent outcomes for millions of customers. description: About the role This is a hands-on IT management role . A global medical device company needs an onsite IT manager for its R&D labs in Yokneam : the person who keeps the labs' computers, servers, networks and lab instruments' connections running, secure and compliant, handles IT support for the lab teams, and manages the outside IT vendors. The client calls the role "Service Delivery Lead". In practice: IT support and operations (tickets in ServiceNow, ITIL processes, SLAs), infrastructure (servers, backups, patching), networking and security (firewalls, separated lab networks, connecting instrument PCs and controllers), and working within medical-industry regulation (audits, change control). Long-term, full-time position, onsite in Yokneam five days a week. What you will do Run day-to-day IT support and operations for the R&D labs, together with the site's IT and R&D leaders: incidents, requests, problems and changes, managed in ServiceNow according to ITIL, against clear SLAs. Find and fix root causes, and keep site leadership informed. Be the site's go-to IT person: turn R&D needs into practical, secure solutions in the labs, and advise on the right systems and architecture. Own the lab networking and security: firewalls, separated (segmented / ICE) lab networks, IT/OT and IoT integration, and network connections for instrument PCs, controllers and gateways. Keep the site's asset list and locally managed applications documented. Manage the lab infrastructure (servers, networks, software baselines, backups and disaster recovery), and coordinate patching, hardening and vulnerability fixes on instrument workstations within regulatory limits. Work with Lab Operations, Quality, Engineering, Cybersecurity and vendors to turn lab needs into scalable, secure solutions. Manage vendor performance and onsite work. Keep the site compliant with GxP and data-integrity requirements (GAMP 5, ALCOA+), and support audits, CAPAs, deviations and change control for computerized systems. Prepare the site for projects such as lab moves, new instruments and integrations, including network segmentation (ISA-95, NIST), connectivity, and the effect on qualification and validation. Improve processes continually (simplify, automate, standardize, reduce cost), report through KPI dashboards and service reviews, and maintain clear knowledge articles and runbooks. What you bring A bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience. 6+ years in IT operations, IT support management or IT infrastructure, including hands-on support of scientific, R&D, lab or industrial (OT) environments (instrument PCs, controllers, data systems). Hands-on experience with ITIL-based service management tools (ServiceNow, Jira). Strong practical knowledge of firewalls, segmented networks and secure equipment connectivity in regulated settings. description: Description Annapurna Labs builds the custom silicon and software behind AWS, including the AWS Nitro System, Graviton, and the Inferentia/Trainium machine learning accelerators. That software runs on millions of AWS servers and supports every EC2 customer. The role We're looking for a Senior TPM to drive large, cross-team software programs from planning through production. You'll work with engineering teams in Israel and the US, and with AWS service teams. You'll turn ambiguous goals into clear plans, own software release and deployment programs, and raise how well the org delivers. This is a technical role: you'll go deep on architecture, dependencies and tradeoffs with engineers and senior leaders. Key job responsibilities Own multi-team software programs end to end: new feature development, major releases, and fleet-wide deployments. Define scope, milestones, dependencies and success metrics with engineering managers and principal engineers. Run the program cadence: roadmaps, schedules, risk tracking, status reviews and launch readiness. Own the software release process: release planning, quality gates, branching and versioning, and go/no-go decisions. Drive safe deployment to the AWS fleet with service teams: rollout plans, monitoring and rollback readiness. Find risks early, lead tradeoff decisions on scope, schedule and quality, and escalate clearly. Improve how engineering works through better processes, tools and metrics (CI/CD, test coverage, delivery speed, operational excellence). Write clear narratives (PR/FAQs, 6-pagers, program and operational reviews) for leadership up to VP level. A day in the life Your morning might start with a sync between the driver and firmware teams, where you sort out a dependency that's putting the next release at risk. You'll update the plan and agree on next steps before lunch. Midday, you might join an architecture review with principal engineers on a new feature. You'll ask questions about scope, test strategy and rollout risk, and turn the discussion into milestones the teams can commit to. In the afternoon, you could be leading a go/no-go meeting for a software release. You'll review quality gates, test results and open issues, then coordinate a safe, gradual rollout across the AWS fleet with partner service teams. You'll finish the day writing a short program update for leadership: what's on track, what's at risk, and the decisions you need from them. Some days you'll write a PR/FAQ or 6-pager for a new initiative. On others you'll work with US-based teams in the evening to keep global work moving. No two weeks look the same. One week you're supporting bring-up of new hardware, the next you're improving the CI/CD pipeline or running an operational review after an incident. The common thread is that you own outcomes, not just schedules. מעולמות הנדל"ן, המסחר והתעשייה. תחומי אחריות מרכזיים: הובלה וניהול צוות תכנון ורישוי : סמכות מקצועית וחונכת לצוות, יצירת סטנדרטיזציה, הטמעת תהליכי עבודה סדורים וגיבוש מתודולוגיית Best Practice מחלקתית. נ יהול תהליכי הרישוי מקצה לקצה: אחריות מלאה על כלל תהליכי הרישוי וההיתרים בחברה – החל משלב הגשת הבקשה למידע ועד לקבלת היתר בנייה ותעודת גמר. שילוב בין ראייה אסטרטגית לעבודת Hands-On: ידע ויכולת לנוע בין תמונת רוחב ואסטרטגיה לבין ירידה לפרטים הקטנים, הובלת תהליכים רוחביים לצד ניהול פרויקטים אסטרטגיים, נכונות לפתרון בעיות בשטח ופתרון חסמים בזמן אמת. ניתוח תכנוני וסטטוטורי: מיפוי וניתוח שטחים פוטנציאליים למיזמי אנרגיה מתחדשת ואגירה. ניהול תקציבי: אחריות מלאה לעמידה בתקציבי הייזום והתכנון של הפרויקטים. ניהול ממשקים פנים-ארגוניים: עבודה צמודה ושוטפת מול צוותי פיתוח עסקי, אופרציה, הנדסה, פרויקטים, אינטרקונקשן וגורמי ניהול נוספים. עבודה מול גורמים ויועצים חיצוניים: הובלת עבודת היועצים (עורכי בקשה, אדריכלים, יועצים משפטיים, יועצי סביבה ויועצים מקצועיים בתחום התכנון והבנייה). עבודה מול גופים סטטוטוריים: ניהול מערכות יחסים ועבודה שוטפת מול ועדות לתכנון ובנייה, מהנדסי ועדות, ועדות מחוזיות, רשות מקרקעי ישראל (רמ"י) ורשויות מקומיות. דרישות: תואר ראשון – חובה, תואר ראשון עם אוריינטציה הנדסית/ אדריכלית – יתרון. ניסיון מקצועי: ניסיון של 3 שנים לפחות בניהול תהליכי תכנון ורישוי, לרבות הובלה והפקה של היתרי בנייה – חובה. ניסיון ניהולי: ניסיון בהובלה, חניכה וניהול צוותים – חובה. עבודה מול רשויות: ניסיון מוכח בעבודה מול רשויות מקומיות, ועדות מקומיות וגופים סטטוטוריים – חובה. ניסיון בתחום: ניסיון בעבודה בתחום האנרגיה המתחדשת/אגירה בישראל – יתרון משמעותי. כישורים אישיים ומקצועיים: יחסי אנוש מעולים, יכולת הובלה, חניכה וגישה פרואקטיבית ("Can-Do Attitude"). חשיבה אסטרטגית ומערכתית לצד ירידה לפרטים, סדר, ארגון ויכולת מעקב גבוהה. יכולת מוכחת להסרת חסמים, קיצור זמנים והובלת תהליכים מורכבים במקביל. כישורי תקשורת, ניסוח וביטוי ברמה גבוהה (בכתב ובעל פה). יכולת גבוהה ליצירת אמון, רתימה ועבודה מול שותפים עסקיים וממשקים מרובים. היקף המשרה: מלאה. המשרה כוללת רכב ודורשת נסיעות ברחבי הארץ.
title: מנהל/ת מחלקת תכנון ורישוי פרויקטים

description: At DCG - a solution-creator, we redefine Cyber Intelligence, Cyber Defense and Homeland Security (HLS) with innovative, field proven solutions. description: Parallel Wireless is reimagining mobile networks with innovative, energy-efficient Open RAN solutions. Join us as we lead the future of telecommunications, driving innovation through green and sustainable networks . Learn more about our mission, vision and values . People come to work at Parallel Wireless because we are building the future of telecom. They stay because they are challenged and driven by an incredible product and team. We take pride in our commitment to employee development, and our culture fosters an atmosphere of empowerment, trust, respect, and communication. Lead the outdoor (field) test activities for Parallel Wireless's wireless telecom and cloud-based 4G/5G ORAN solutions. The work location is in Israel and combines hands-on testing at outdoor sites in the field with lab work and close collaboration with R&D, product and test engineers across Parallel Wireless sites. As the senior engineer on the team, you'll own the outdoor test domain end-to-end — from defining the field test strategy and building the outdoor setups, through running drive and walk tests on live deployments, to analyzing RF/KPI results and driving issues to root cause with R&D. You will also mentor the team's junior test engineers and represent the outdoor test activity in front of customers during field trials and acceptance. Job Responsibilities: Lead and own the outdoor/field test activities of the team: plan, schedule and execute drive tests, walk tests and field trials of Parallel Wireless 4G/5G ORAN products (radio units, DU/CU and core) in real-world outdoor deployments. Define the outdoor test strategy, test plans, test cases and acceptance criteria covering coverage, capacity, throughput, latency, mobility (handover/cell reselection), interference and KPI benchmarking against 3GPP and customer requirements. Design and build outdoor end-to-end test setups: site survey and selection, antenna and RF path, backhaul, power, GPS/timing, UE fleet and measurement tools. Execute field measurement campaigns with drive-test tools and scanners, and analyze RF and performance KPIs (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, throughput, BLER, latency, call/session drops, handover success rate). Analyze and debug UE, RAN and core logs collected in the field and resolve issues in outdoor setups (For Ex: UE/mobile issues, RF/antenna/fiber connectivity, backhaul, power and timing, etc.); isolate RF, baseband, configuration and software issues and drive them to root cause together with R&D. Analyze, reproduce and validate customer field-found defects and take part in customer trials and field acceptance tests. Produce clear field test reports and KPI summaries and present findings to R&D, product management and customers. Mentor and guide junior test engineers; review their test plans, setups and results. Suggest improvements and changes to the product in order to improve customer experience. Automation: Define requirements for automating field data collection, KPI post-processing and report

Over the past year, frontier models have reached systems they were never meant to access, making the safe evaluation of agent behavior a critical discipline in its own right. Innodata’s Agentic Evaluation and Safety practice works with the world’s leading AI labs to address these challenges. We are hiring a Head of AI Cyber Agentic Environments and Testing to build and lead the team creating realistic, fully contained cyber ranges and simulated enterprise environments where frontier agents are tested for offensive capability, misuse, and misaligned behavior before deployment. This is a rare opportunity to lead at the frontier of AI cyber safety, partnering with alignment researchers, reporting directly to the CTO, and building a world-class global team in a rapidly emerging field. What you'll do: Push the frontier of AI cyber testing Define how frontier agents are tested for offensive cyber capability and misuse. Cover whether an agent will execute exploits it encounters, chain vulnerabilities across applications and VMs, or leak sensitive data mid-task. Design cyber ranges and vulnerable-by-design enterprise environments: web apps, identity systems, Active Directory, CI/CD, cloud consoles. They should be realistic enough that a frontier model cannot tell it is being tested. Build the instrumentation that makes results trustworthy: tripwires, honeytokens, canary credentials, full action telemetry, and state-diff grading. Own containment as a first-class engineering discipline. Every environment is hermetic, egress is provably zero, and isolation is tested, not assumed.
